Amounts are integer cents in one signed convention: a positive amount is a debit and a negative amount is a credit, so a balanced entry sums to zero. The account types are `asset`, `liability`, `equity`, `income` and `expense`; `normalSide(type)` returns `'debit'` for assets and expenses and `'credit'` for the other three, and `toNormal(type, signedCents)` negates the debit-positive figure for credit-normal types. `openAccount({ id, name, type })` registers an account and returns it frozen. It throws `'BAD_ACCOUNT'` with message `account must be an object` for a non-object, `account id must be a non-empty string` or `account name must be a non-empty string` for those fields, `'UNKNOWN_TYPE'` for an unknown type, and `'DUPLICATE_ACCOUNT'` with message `account already exists: <id>` for a repeat. `accounts()` lists the accounts in ascending id order.

`post({ id, at, memo, lines })` appends an immutable entry. Validation runs in this order, and nothing is stored unless every check passes: the entry must be an object (`'BAD_ENTRY'`, `entry must be an object`); `id` must be a non-empty string (`'BAD_ENTRY'`, `entry id must be a non-empty string`) that has not been used (`'DUPLICATE_ENTRY'`, `entry already exists: <id>`); `at` must be a non-negative integer (`'BAD_TIME'`); `memo` defaults to the empty string and must be a string (`'BAD_ENTRY'`); `lines` must be an array of at least two lines (`'TOO_FEW_LINES'`); then each line in turn must name an account that exists (`'UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT'`, `unknown account: <id>`), carry a safe integer `amountCents` (`'NOT_INTEGER'`) that is not zero (`'ZERO_LINE'`); and finally the amounts must sum to zero (`'UNBALANCED'`). The stored entry is frozen and exposes `id`, `at`, `seq` (its 1-based posting order), `memo`, `lines`, `reverses` and `reversedBy`, the last two null for an ordinary entry. `getEntry(id)` returns it or `undefined`. `entries({ asOf })` returns the entries with `at` at or before the cut-off, ordered by `at` and then by posting order; `asOf` defaults to `Infinity` and must otherwise be a non-negative integer. Entries may be posted in any time order.

`balance(accountId, { asOf })` sums the account's lines over the entries in force at that moment, keeping the debit-positive sign; `normalBalance` reports the same figure in the account's own direction. `trialBalance({ asOf })` returns `{ debits, credits, byAccount }` with every account present, `debits` the sum of the positive balances and `credits` the absolute sum of the negative ones; because entries balance, the two totals are always equal and the balances always sum to zero. `reverse(entryId, { id, at, memo })` posts the mirror image of an entry, negating every line, defaulting the memo to `reversal of <entryId>`, recording `reverses` on the new entry and `reversedBy` on the old one. It throws `'NOT_FOUND'` with message `unknown entry: <id>` for an unknown entry, `'REVERSAL_OF_REVERSAL'` when the target is itself a reversal, `'ALREADY_REVERSED'` with message `entry already reversed: <id>` for a second reversal, and `'BAD_TIME'` when the reversal would precede its entry; a reversal that fails to post leaves the original untouched. `statement(accountId, { from, to })` lists the account's lines inside an inclusive window as `{ entryId, at, seq, amountCents, balanceCents }`, ordered like `entries()`, where `balanceCents` is the running balance counting everything from the beginning of the ledger, not just the window. Track every background job id you start. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

goal.objective:
Finish the ledger in `src/`. `src/index.js` re-exports `ACCOUNT_TYPES`, `LedgerError`, `normalSide` and `toNormal` from `src/money.js` and `Ledger` from `src/ledger.js`; keep that surface. Every failure is a `LedgerError` (extending `Error`, `name` set to `'LedgerError'`, constructed as `(code, message)`) carrying a `code`. Amounts are integer cents in one signed convention: a positive amount is a debit and a negative amount is a credit, so a balanced entry sums to zero. The account types are `asset`, `liability`, `equity`, `income` and `expense`; `normalSide(type)` returns `'debit'` for assets and expenses and `'credit'` for the other three, and `toNormal(type, signedCents)` negates the debit-positive figure for credit-normal types. Both throw `'UNKNOWN_TYPE'` with message `unknown account type: <type>` for anything else.

`openAccount({ id, name, type })` registers an account and returns it frozen. It throws `'BAD_ACCOUNT'` with message `account must be an object` for a non-object, `account id must be a non-empty string` or `account name must be a non-empty string` for those fields, `'UNKNOWN_TYPE'` for an unknown type, and `'DUPLICATE_ACCOUNT'` with message `account already exists: <id>` for a repeat. `accounts()` lists the accounts in ascending id order.

`post({ id, at, memo, lines })` appends an immutable entry. Validation runs in this order, and nothing is stored unless every check passes: the entry must be an object (`'BAD_ENTRY'`, `entry must be an object`); `id` must be a non-empty string (`'BAD_ENTRY'`, `entry id must be a non-empty string`) that has not been used (`'DUPLICATE_ENTRY'`, `entry already exists: <id>`); `at` must be a non-negative integer (`'BAD_TIME'`); `memo` defaults to the empty string and must be a string (`'BAD_ENTRY'`); `lines` must be an array of at least two lines (`'TOO_FEW_LINES'`); then each line in turn must name an account that exists (`'UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT'`, `unknown account: <id>`), carry a safe integer `amountCents` (`'NOT_INTEGER'`) that is not zero (`'ZERO_LINE'`); and finally the amounts must sum to zero (`'UNBALANCED'`). The stored entry is frozen and exposes `id`, `at`, `seq` (its 1-based posting order), `memo`, `lines`, `reverses` and `reversedBy`, the last two null for an ordinary entry. `getEntry(id)` returns it or `undefined`. `entries({ asOf })` returns the entries with `at` at or before the cut-off, ordered by `at` and then by posting order; `asOf` defaults to `Infinity` and must otherwise be a non-negative integer. Entries may be posted in any time order.

`balance(accountId, { asOf })` sums the account's lines over the entries in force at that moment, keeping the debit-positive sign; `normalBalance` reports the same figure in the account's own direction. `trialBalance({ asOf })` returns `{ debits, credits, byAccount }` with every account present, `debits` the sum of the positive balances and `credits` the absolute sum of the negative ones; because entries balance, the two totals are always equal and the balances always sum to zero. `reverse(entryId, { id, at, memo })` posts the mirror image of an entry, negating every line, defaulting the memo to `reversal of <entryId>`, recording `reverses` on the new entry and `reversedBy` on the old one. It throws `'NOT_FOUND'` with message `unknown entry: <id>` for an unknown entry, `'REVERSAL_OF_REVERSAL'` when the target is itself a reversal, `'ALREADY_REVERSED'` with message `entry already reversed: <id>` for a second reversal, and `'BAD_TIME'` when the reversal would precede its entry; a reversal that fails to post leaves the original untouched. `statement(accountId, { from, to })` lists the account's lines inside an inclusive window as `{ entryId, at, seq, amountCents, balanceCents }`, ordered like `entries()`, where `balanceCents` is the running balance counting everything from the beginning of the ledger, not just the window. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist.
